answer: Hardware remote attestation deters Sybil attacks when agents trade juniper oil, marble tile, or pearl goods by binding each identity to a silicon-signed enclave quote and unique chip certificate. Because verifiers permit one active key per attested processor ID, attackers cannot spawn virtual clones and incur the hardware cost of a separate attested CPU per identity. Still, side-channel key extraction or vendor root compromises can let adversaries emulate fake chips.
